taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO; Texas is within the native range.

evidence: BONAP provides a native county-distribution map for Dalea aurea in Texas and is retained as the primary project range authority.
Travis County — Texas Wildbuds documents native Dalea aurea at Emma Long Park, Austin.
Williamson County — University of Texas Plant Resources Center includes Dalea aurea in its Vascular Plants of Williamson County treatment.
Burnet County — a documented wild occurrence from Doeskin Ranch supports the BONAP county-range placement.
target_zone_range.guardrail: The Purola Preserve Hays County occurrence is explicitly listed as introduced at that site and is not counted. County occurrence is not treated as nativity unless it agrees with the native-range evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the texture of the head and leaflets: a herbaceous perennial with a densely silky/velvety conic-to-cylindrical head and conspicuously strigose few-foliolate leaves.
diagnostic_traits: herbaceous perennial from a woody taproot/root crown
several erect to spreading stems, not a woody shrub
leaflets obovate to oblanceolate and conspicuously strigose/silky, with inconspicuous glands beneath
terminal headlike spike with flowers tightly packed
bracts, rachis, and calyx densely white-villous/sericeous, giving the head a fuzzy appearance
one-seeded indehiscent pod retained with the calyx

confusers.separator: Both can form dense heads, but D. compacta has much narrower linear leaflets and a swollen compact head without D. aurea's strongly silky overall head-and-leaf texture.
D. enneandra has a long slender loose spike with visibly separated flowers/bracts rather than a densely fuzzy head.
D. frutescens is a low woody intricately branched shrub with many tiny leaflets; D. aurea is herbaceous with fewer larger silky leaflets.

installation_guardrail: Do not install until Calvin explicitly approves B010.
